description: Canonical list of leading tokens that mark a cite-key's author slot (or a bold/OCR token mistaken for a first author) as an article-structure / section-header / analyte / common-noun artifact rather than a real author surname. The auto/OCR ingest builds keys as `<first-author><year>-<title-slug>`; when it cannot find a real surname it grabs the first salient word it sees (a section header, a bolded title word, an analyte name), producing keys like `abstract2021-...`, `keywords2019-...`, `arsenic2023-...`. This file is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH consumed by tools/lib/cite-key-validity.mjs (which tools/audit-doi-collisions.mjs and the ingest gates import) and by tools/build-triage-manifest.py (extract_first_author). Keep it in sync across all three — do NOT fork the list. Only add tokens that are NEVER plausible as a real first-author surname (avoid words that are also common surnames, e.g. Taylor, Francis, Page, Bell).
